questions.question: What is a direct consequence of adopting Spec-Driven Development (SDD) when creating enterprise-grade agents?

options.answer: Developers must spend more time holding complex API references, such as the full ADK graph routing, in their active memory.
Evaluation datasets must be written manually using strict string-matching assertions rather than LLM-as-judge metrics.
The generated codebase becomes the derivative of the SDD, which means it becomes easier to regenerate if the specification is solid.
options.explanation: Correct! Because the high-quality specification acts as the source of truth, you can recreate or restructure the entire codebase at any time without losing your core design intent.

options.answer: The coding agent becomes restricted to using older 1.x SequentialAgent composition models rather than graph structures.

questions.question: When evaluating agent quality using the toolchain, what advantage does an LLM-as-judge metric have over traditional code unit tests?

options.answer: It provides a quantitative score that guarantees the local development backend is listening directly on the host operating system.
It automatically tightens the configuration definitions in the project's layout files to prevent server crashes.
It completely eliminates the requirement to execute both generation and grading steps when validating code changes.
It can qualitatively grade the entire execution trace and trajectory of an agent rather than relying on brittle string-matching assertions.
options.explanation: Correct! Because agents deal with probabilistic behavior and qualitative judgment, an LLM-as-judge can assess whether the overall behavior and routing outcomes matched your policy intent.

questions.question: How do the available authentication paths for the development toolchain impact the capabilities of an ambient agent during local execution?

options.answer: Google Cloud credentials provide access to Vertex AI services for session state management, whereas a Gemini API key serves as a fallback path.
options.explanation: Correct! Google Cloud credentials unlock advanced features like the Vertex AI Session Service for human-in-the-loop state management across sessions, while a Gemini API key acts as a quick starting alternative.

options.answer: A Gemini API key is required to build graph workflows, whereas Google Cloud credentials are restricted to standalone terminal checks.
Exporting a Gemini API key automatically pins the toolchain binary version across all team members in the pyproject.toml file.
Using Google Cloud credentials forces the environment setup command to install the seven skill files globally, while an API key installs them locally.

questions.question: When leveraging the Agent Development Kit (ADK) 2.0 API to build an agent, how is the architecture fundamentally structured to separate deterministic logic from qualitative judgment?

options.answer: As an isolated set of unit tests that utilize standard regex definitions to enforce security checkpoints across multiple chat applications.
As a conversational interface that relies entirely on an interactive playground to route user messages asynchronously.
As a sequential prompt chain where the language model dynamically evaluates numerical conditions and routing logic on every turn.
As a graph workflow where function nodes handle deterministic business rules in code, and specific model-backed nodes are reserved for interpretation.
options.explanation: That's correct. ADK 2.0 uses a graph Workflow API where straightforward rules (like a dollar threshold) stay reliably in Python code, ensuring language models are only queried when genuine interpretation is required.

questions.question: What capability does an ADK trigger endpoint provide when transforming a graph workflow into an event-driven ambient service?

options.answer: It allows an agent to bypass the human-in-the-loop pause step whenever a prompt-injection attempt is flagged.
It automatically handles the incoming message plumbing, decodes the payload, and instantiates a routed, stateful run.
options.explanation: Correct! Trigger endpoints eliminate the need to hand-write server integration logic by automatically receiving external events (like Pub/Sub messages) and mapping them into standard agent runs.

options.answer: It forces the judge model to use standard string-matching assertions rather than qualitative scoring rubrics.
It enables the interactive local developer interface to hot-reload and display execution traces inside a chat window.

questions.question: Why is it highly recommended to apply the session-start pattern at the beginning of every interaction with your development platform?

options.answer: It triggers a global download that automatically re-installs and overwrites the active environment dependencies using uv sync.
It anchors the conversation on the correct API surface, preventing the agent from losing context and defaulting to deprecated 1.x composition models.
options.explanation: Correct! Long conversations can dilute context window details. Running a session-start prompt ensures the agent explicitly loads the correct 2.0 graph references from the start.

options.answer: It bypasses the bounded workspace restrictions so the agent can modify configuration files outside the project directory without permission.
It converts the agent's internal operating model from a single-turn architecture to an interactive web application.
